note: Merged/ready real issue about claim-staleness diagnostics; today's A4 limited_scope criterion false-positives on its own diagnostic-signal prose (known lexical-gate boundary gap).
title: Surface a heartbeat-overdue-but-not-stale diagnostic signal for claimed issues
body:
## Background

Field evidence from a live investigation on 2026-07-16 (~22:48 UTC): 9 open
execution-leaf issues (#1387, #1389, #1394, #1396, #1398, #1399, #1401,
#1402, #1419) were actively claimed by distinct concurrent sessions, ages
ranging ~13h-19h — all under the 24h `claimTiming.staleAge` transfer
threshold, so none were takeover-eligible, and per
`idd-resume-stall.instructions.md` S3 the correct (and only) action for an
observer was "hold and stop, do not post" — which is what happened; nothing
was mutated by the investigation itself.

However, every one of the 9 claims had already passed the 12h
`claimTiming.heartbeatInterval` with **zero heartbeat re-post**, and every
one showed **zero commits ahead of `main`** and had **never been pushed** to
a remote branch (`git log main..HEAD` empty in each sibling worktree,
`git branch -vv` shows no upstream, and `gh pr list --state open` returned
zero PRs repository-wide at the time). A 4-issue comment-timeline sample
showed an identical shape: claim to a B2/plan comment within ~15 minutes,
then complete silence for 13-19+ hours. 6 of the 9 worktrees had a fully
clean tree matching `main` exactly (no local edits beyond the initial
checkout); the other 3 had substantial **uncommitted, unpushed** diffs
matching their issue's scope (84/186/426 changed lines) — real work started,
then stopped cold with not even a WIP commit.

Every claim-state-annotating surface in this repository currently exposes
only a **binary** signal: `discover-roadmap-graph.mjs --with-claim-state`
and `discover-orphan-filter.mjs --with-claim-state` both emit `activeClaim:
{ present, stale, claimId, agentId }` — `stale` is the hard 24h line only.
Nothing surfaces the **intermediate** state this investigation exposed:
"claimed, past the documented heartbeat interval, zero heartbeat, zero
branch-tip movement" — objectively derivable from data these helpers already
fetch (the claim's `created_at`, `claimTiming.heartbeatInterval` from
config, and the sibling remote branch's existence/tip), yet invisible until
the hard stale line is crossed. `scripts/stalled-session-quiet-check.mjs`
(the existing S2 quiet-window helper) is the closest existing tool but
requires `--pr <number>`, so it has no equivalent for the **pre-push** state
that 6 of the 9 observed cases were actually in.

This is a diagnostic-visibility gap, not a safety-gate gap: the 24h
`stale`-threshold takeover rule in `idd-resume-stall.instructions.md` S3
("Claim age < 24h: hold and stop") is a deliberate, correct safety design
and is explicitly **out of scope to change** here.

## Proposed change

Add a computed, informational field to the `activeClaim` object emitted by
`discover-roadmap-graph.mjs --with-claim-state` and
`discover-orphan-filter.mjs --with-claim-state`:

- `heartbeatOverdue: boolean` — `true` when `(now - latest valid
  claimed-by/heartbeat created_at) >= claimTiming.heartbeatInterval` and no
  later trusted heartbeat comment exists; `false` otherwise (including when
  `present` is `false`).
- Purely additive: existing `present` / `stale` / `claimId` / `agentId`
  fields and their semantics are unchanged. The new field is emitted
  unconditionally alongside them whenever `--with-claim-state` is already
  passed (no new flag) so existing byte-shape expectations for the
  flag-absent case are unaffected.
- Mirror the advisory-note pattern already established by #1398's
  `baseAdvancedSinceMergeBase`: a new evidence field that never changes
  existing gating semantics or return-value shape when the underlying
  condition is false.

Document the signal in `idd-resume-stall.instructions.md` (near S2/S3) and
`idd-overview-core.instructions.md`'s heartbeat section: a missed heartbeat
past `claimTiming.heartbeatInterval` is an expected, human-visible
diagnostic worth a glance or a live-status digest note, but by itself
**never** authorizes any autonomous takeover action before the S3 24h line —
state this explicitly so a future reader does not conflate the two.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `discover-roadmap-graph.mjs --with-claim-state` and
      `discover-orphan-filter.mjs --with-claim-state` emit `activeClaim.
      heartbeatOverdue` per the derivation above.
- [ ] Unit tests (injected fixtures, no live network) cover: overdue-true,
      overdue-false (within window), overdue-false (no active claim), and
      overdue-false-because-heartbeat-was-reposted.
- [ ] Existing `present` / `stale` / `claimId` / `agentId` fields and
      values are unchanged for every existing test fixture (no regression).
- [ ] `idd-resume-stall.instructions.md` and
      `idd-overview-core.instructions.md` document the signal and explicitly
      state it does not change the S3 24h takeover gate.
- [ ] `docs/idd-helper-scripts.md` documents the new field for both
      helpers.
- [ ] `pnpm run build` output committed; existing tests pass;
      `node scripts/audit-docs.mjs --check` reports zero drift.

## Follow-up issues (out of scope here)

- Extending `scripts/stalled-session-quiet-check.mjs` (or an equivalent) to
  cover the **pre-push** quiet-window case using worktree/branch-tip
  evidence instead of PR/CI activity, so the same quiet-window concept
  applies before a branch is ever pushed. This is materially more design
  work than the additive field above and is left for separate scoping.
- Whether/how `resume-claim-routing.mjs` (a different output shape:
  `active_claim: { agent_id, claim_id, created_at, branch }`, no
  `stale`/`heartbeatOverdue` fields today) should gain an equivalent signal
  is likewise left for separate scoping rather than assumed here.
